title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 405-408 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck studies a group scheme M_{ρ,σ} over Z. It is apparently built from SL(2), or rather a form SG of it, together with the tori T_ρ and T_σ attached to the elliptic elements ρ (order 6, with (Z+Zρ)^* = Z/6) and σ (order 4, with (Z+Zσ)^* = Z/4). These are the generators in the amalgam SL(2,Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. M_{ρ,σ} is a semi-direct product M_{ρ,σ}(0)·SG, where M_{ρ,σ}(0) = T_{ρ,σ} (also written Γ_{ρ,σ}) is the subgroup scheme of triples (u,a,b) in T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ satisfying a determinant condition. N'_σ is the normaliser of T_σ.

On the previous page he computed T_{ρ,σ}(Z) ≅ Z/6 × D_4, where D_4 = {1,τ_∞}·Z/4 is the dihedral group of order 8 ('symétries du carré', which he calls 'd'ordre 4').

On this page:
- He identifies the element realising r_0 = τ'_∞, r_1 = -τ'_0, r_∞ = τ_∞ with (1,τ_∞) in Z/6 × D_4.
- (43) He deduces M_{ρ,σ}(Z) ≅ T_{ρ,σ}(Z) ⋉ SL(2,Z), where T_{ρ,σ}(Z) is identified with M_{ρ,σ}(0)(Z), i.e. ≅ (Z/6 × D_4) ⋉ SL(2,Z).
- (44) The action factors through the projection Z/6 × D_4 → D_4 → D_4/(Z/4) = {1,τ_∞}. Here τ_∞ acts on SL(2,Z) by conjugation by diag(-1,1), which is the standard outer automorphism of SL(2,Z) induced from GL(2,Z); it sends σ to σ^{-1}.
- (45) The canonical homomorphism M_{ρ,σ} → μ_2 × μ_2 (two determinant characters) factors through T_{ρ,σ}. On Z-points it is trivial on Z/6 × Z/4, where Z/4 = D_4^+ is the rotation subgroup with determinant 1. It sends τ_∞ to (-1,-1).
- Hence the image on Z-points is the diagonal {±(1,1)}, so M_{ρ,σ}(Z) → (μ_2×μ_2)(Z) is not surjective, even though the map is presumably an epimorphism of group schemes.

The next page goes on to compute the centre of M_{ρ,σ}. The whole computation serves to describe the integral points of the group scheme whose Z-points 'model' SL(2,Z) together with its marked elliptic tori. This belongs to the genus-0/1 Teichmüller-tower and 'lacets' equation programme.
errors: (43)-(44) as written in the image read (Z/4Z × D_4)·SL(2,Z), whereas the previous page and (45) on this same page give T_{ρ,σ}(Z) ≅ Z/6Z × D_4. Z/4 should be Z/6 here; this is a slip.

D_4 is called 'diédral d'ordre 4' on the previous page; it is the dihedral group of order 8 (symmetries of the square), so '4' refers to the square, not the order. This is a harmless naming convention.

ideas.what: Integral points of the group scheme M_{ρ,σ} as a semi-direct product (Z/6 × D_4) ⋉ SL(2,Z), with action through the outer automorphism conj by diag(-1,1)
ideas.modern_name: semi-direct product with the GL2(Z)/SL2(Z) outer automorphism; normalisers of elliptic tori in GL2 over Z

ideas.what: Determinant map M_{ρ,σ} → μ_2×μ_2 is not surjective on Z-points (image is the diagonal)
ideas.modern_name: failure of surjectivity on integral points of an fppf epimorphism / component groups

deep.surprise_reason: A routine explicit computation of integral points and a determinant character in an auxiliary group-scheme model of SL(2,Z) with its elliptic elements. The computation is correct apart from a Z/4 vs Z/6 slip, and contains nothing beyond standard facts.
transcription_corrections: In (43) the 'fraction' T_{ρ,σ}(Z) / M_{ρ,σ(0)}(Z) is not a quotient. It is T_{ρ,σ}(Z) underlined with the annotation M_{ρ,σ}(0)(Z) beneath, i.e. an identification T_{ρ,σ}(Z) = M_{ρ,σ}(0)(Z).
Similarly 'Z/4Z / D_4^+' is Z/4Z underlined with D_4^+ beneath, meaning Z/4Z = D_4^+ (the rotation subgroup), not a quotient.
Line 2 likely reads 'de r_0=τ'_∞, r_1=-τ'_0, r_∞=τ_∞ correspondant à l'élément (1,τ_∞)'.
The word read as 'question' in line 1 may be 'nécessairement'/'possible'; it is illegible.
Last line: 'Ceci prouve donc que cet homom sur les pts entiers n'est' (continuing 'pas surjectif' on the next page).
